key_insight: ProofPatch helps humans review whether Lean statements express their intent, then tracks when formalization changes require those judgments to be revisited.
engineering_relevance: It adds semantic change tracking and declaration pinning to protect reviewed formal specifications during human or LLM-driven edits.
method: Use kernel-checked probes to investigate unnecessary hypotheses or possible counterexamples.
Store review decisions with fingerprints of elaborated statements and their dependencies, rather than source text.
Revisit affected decisions after semantic changes and block patches that alter pinned declarations.
evidence_signal: Across 229 Mathlib revision pairs, ProofPatch flagged 118 of 12,898 synthetic decisions for re-review; kernel evidence achieved 0.88–0.96 precision on 1,527 labeled statements, and no pinned-statement change passed in 344 LLM-agent runs.
watch_item: Kernel evidence supports human judgment but cannot establish that a formal statement captures its intended meaning; the change-tracking evaluation used synthetic review decisions.
paper_title: ProofPatch: Reviewing Lean Statements and Keeping the Reviews Valid as Formalizations Evolve
